reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm whether the TCR gene-engineered lymphocytes successfully engaged gp100 on melanoma cells. Without target engagement evidence, cannot confirm the first step of the causal chain. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess whether T-cell activation and tumor antigen recognition occurred as intended. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint of clinical tumor regression by RECIST was not met. Overall response rate was only 19% (4/21 patients), which is modest for this indication. No p-value reported and no statistical significance achieved. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Limited subgroup analysis showed PBL arm had higher response rate (3/19, 15.8%) compared to TIL arm (1/2, 50%), but sample sizes are too small to draw meaningful conclusions. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial had very high incidence of serious adverse events (>50% of patients experienced SAEs including hypotension 10.5%, renal failure 10.5%, acute vascular leak syndrome 10.5%, creatinine elevation 15.8%). The investigator noted 'low accrual' suggesting recruitment challenges. Small sample size (n=21) may have contributed to underpowering.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker data available to assess target engagement or pathway modulation. Cannot determine if failure was due to lack of target engagement, inadequate biological response, or other factors.
Small sample size of 21 patients with investigator commentary noting 'low accrual' suggests the trial may have been underpowered to detect treatment effects.

edges_to_update.reasoning: Primary endpoint was measured (19% ORR) but without historical comparator or statistical significance, cannot determine if this level of response translates to clinical benefit in metastatic melanoma

review_reason: No biomarker or target engagement data available to assess mechanistic failure mode. High SAE rate and small sample size create multiple confounding factors that prevent clear mechanistic classification.
